sheep_herdwick.text: How did YOU get up here? I came for the grass. The cairn is an accident.

ld_shepherd.text: The Herdwicks 'heft' to the hill: each ewe knows her own bit of fell without a fence, and she passes it to her lambs. If a flock's lost, you can't just replace it. You have to wait three generations.
My dog's name is Fly. She knows more about the sheep than I do, and she's polite about it.

then.text: Eight. Seven on the fell, and the one on the summit who thinks she's a mountain goat. That's what I wrote in the book, and the book is never wrong. Fly is never wrong either, but she's a dog.
How many Herdwicks have you counted on the fell?
Eight! The seven on the fell and the one up top! You've sharp eyes. Here, for your trouble. Kendal mint cake: the proper sort, the kind that has seen a mountain.

else.text: Hmm. That's not what Fly says. Have another look: the ones down on the fell, and the awkward one on the very top. All of them count, even the rude ones.
I'm a sheep short in my sums, or one over. Would you count them for me? Every Herdwick on the fell, high and low, then come back and tell me the number.

ld_walker.text: Eight hundred metres up and the weather's changed four times. Waterproofs on, waterproofs off, and now a hat with a bobble. The Lakes make you a layer person.
There's a rule: Wainwright's guides list 214 fells. People try to climb them all. They're called Wainwright-baggers. It's a hobby and also a punishment.

ld_slater.text: Green slate: the colour of rain on a good day. We split it by hand, one layer at a time. You can tell the good bit by the ring when you tap it.
Roofs in the Lakes last a century. Roofing slate's the only thing here that doesn't mind the wet.

ld_poet.text: I wandered lonely as a cloud, but the cloud was quite crowded. Mind you, daffodils do take the day off from the weather.
A famous poet lived near here and walked about 175,000 miles in his life. He wrote his verses in his head as he went. He never once brought a map.

ld_ranger.text: I'm told off for walking off the path, and then I tell off the walkers for walking off the path. It's a very circular job.
Look at the pass in front of you. See the cairn of stones? Please leave them stacked. If you must add one, add a little one.

arts_dove_cottage.text: {greeting} I volunteer at Dove Cottage in Grasmere, where the Wordsworths lived. Eight years, one small house, a sister, a wife, three babies, and Coleridge dropping in at all hours.
Dorothy's journal is the thing. She saw the daffodils first and wrote them down the same night. William took two years to turn it into the poem, and then put in a cloud.
He walked about 175,000 miles in his life, they reckon, composing out loud as he went. The neighbours thought he was talking to himself. He was, in a sense, but it rhymed.

ld_wrestling.text: Cumberland and Westmorland wrestling. Chest to chest, hold locked behind the back, and the first to touch the grass with anything but a boot has lost the fall.
Mind the trunks. Embroidered velvet over long johns, and the wrestlers will tell you the costume wins falls. I've yet to see a pair of trunks throw anyone.
The real thing is Grasmere Sports, every August. Today it's just us and the grass, and it's every bit as damp.
